title: Into the Cool Night
story:
Before James could step out, Barnaby reached into a deep wooden drawer and pulled out a weathered leather strap. With slow, gentle hands, he threaded the strap through the loops of the brass canister, draping it carefully over James's shoulder. James patted the cool metal canister against his flank; it was a comforting weight, the weight of a promise and a destination.

He walked toward the workshop door, his small bare feet silent on the smooth floorboards. He looked back at the ticking brass clocks, each hummed with a different heartbeat. He looked back at the glowing hearth, its embers casting long, lazy shadows across the room. He looked back at Barnaby, who offered a small, encouraging wave from his workbench.

Stepping out into the cool night air of Oakhaven, the contrast was sharp and immediate. The air did not smell of lavender and clock oil; it smelled of damp slate, woodsmoke, and that faint, familiar metallic tang he had first chased down the hillside. The cobblestones beneath his feet were smooth and cold, polished by generations of passing boots.

Ahead, the narrow street wound upward between towering brick buildings, their dark windows reflecting the starlight. Far above the rooftops, the great, silent dome of the Grand Library caught the silver light of the rising moon. James adjusted his new strap, took a deep breath of the night, and took his first step into the sleeping town, wondering if the books inside that dome slept as deeply as the people beneath them.
